answer: An operator-provided no-charge endpoint already exists on this machine: ollama 0.18.3 running as an active systemd service on 127.0.0.1:11434, with five models already pulled. Two of the five are NOT usable for ordinary operation because of their model licences.
consequences_for_maestro: B03's 'select an installed or operator-provided no-charge endpoint' is satisfiable today. The first free adapter should target the ollama HTTP API with qwen2.5-coder:7b (Apache-2.0) as the default coding model and smollm2 as the small/fast route.

B17 made concrete: three of five locally available models carry terms that forbid or restrict ordinary use. A free-mode implementation that simply picked the largest local model would have picked a restricted one. Every enabled model needs its own verification row, exactly like a dependency.

Free mode has no billing penalty but a hard THROUGHPUT budget. At 3.95 generated tok/s, 2,000 tokens of output is about 8 minutes; at 5.5 prompt tok/s, a 20,000-token context manifest costs about an hour just to ingest. Free-mode context budgets are therefore TIGHTER than paid-mode ones, for a different reason.

Cold model load dominated both requests (59.2 s of 71.0 s; 23.1 s of 27.4 s). Model residency, not tokens, is the scarce free-mode resource. A graph that alternates models pays that cost at every switch, and admission must treat 'which model is resident' as a scheduled resource.

Candidate groups, independent test authors and multiple reviewers are the free-mode quality mechanism the plan relies on, and on this hardware they serialise. Free-mode graph width must be admitted against measured tok/s and residency rather than assumed cheap.
